task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: how to identify teammate with closest pre-absence initiation profile
how to define largest gainer and primary types
how reliable are primary type measurements
what sample size is needed for sufficient power
how to control for game context and confounding
own_inferences: The dataset contains only 148 spells across 11 absence cases, which is likely underpowered for detecting medium or small effects. Defining “primary types” and the “closest pre‑absence initiation profile” is methodologically ambiguous and may require complex, potentially unreliable calculations from possession data. The presence of many unmeasured contextual variables (opponent strength, game stage, player roles) introduces high confounding risk. The small sample also limits the ability to perform robust falsification tests or adjust for multiple comparisons.
uncertainties: Exact operational definition of primary offensive types; validity of using minutes or initiations as a proximity metric; measurement noise in possession-level play type data; adequacy of controlling for game context.

historical_effect.explanation: No prior studies were retrieved, so the decision is based solely on methodological assessment of the available data and the research question.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 absence cases provide limited statistical power.
Sparse exposure of each teammate type limits reliable estimation.
Uncertain reliability of primary type classification may bias results.
High potential for unmeasured confounders (game context, opponent strength).

risks.text: Small number of absence cases reduces power.
Sparse exposure of teammates with similar profiles.
Ambiguity in defining and measuring primary types.
Unmeasured contextual variables could bias estimates.

design.estimand: Difference in the change of the absent player’s primary type performance gains attributable to the teammate with the closest pre‑absence initiation profile compared to other teammates.
design.unit: player‑game level change in primary type performance metrics
design.power: Insufficient – expected power < 0.3 for medium effects
design.controls: Game location, opponent strength, game stage, team offensive pace, player roles
design.falsification: Test the same design on positions unrelated to the absent player’s primary types
design.multiplicity: Single primary comparison per absence case; no multiple testing adjustment required
design.decision_rule: Reject null if p<0.05 (but only if sufficient power achieved)
